consensus_summary: Primary consensus meaning is humanity’s inadequate self-made covering for sin and shame (self-righteousness/self-justification), drawn from Adam and Eve’s fig-leaf aprons in Genesis 3:7 and routinely contrasted with God’s later provision of skins; the NT barren-fig-tree motif (leaves without fruit = hypocrisy or empty profession) is a widespread secondary/blended reading.
book_summary: Self-made righteousness — a covering of one’s own cut that is all show and no substance, illustrated by the cursed fig tree that bore leaves but no fruit.
consensus_core_identification: inadequate human self-covering / self-righteousness for sin and shame
book_core_identification: self-made righteousness that is show without substance
boundary_disagreement: None material; the book simply fuses the two motifs already noted as frequently blended in the consensus.
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: both identify fig leaves as self-made/inadequate human covering (self-righteousness). The book’s added phrase “all show and no substance” plus the Matt 21:19 citation merely incorporates the common secondary motif that consensus responses already list and describe as routinely blended with the Genesis covering image; no referent is replaced and no cases are added or excluded.
strongest_objection: A stricter reading could treat the Genesis covering and the NT barren-tree leaves as distinct images that the book equates too tightly, though the consensus itself records the blend as common in preaching.
